tests.description: End-to-end check of one WSM6 sub-time step assembled from the stage components: WSM6Saturation -> WSM6MeltingFreezing -> {WSM6WarmRain, WSM6ColdAccretion, WSM6IceDeposition} -> WSM6MassConservation -> WSM6SaturationAdjustment, coupled by variable_map param_to_var into the stages' `<x>_in` parameters. Reference: WRF 4.8 em_quarter_ss idealized supercell (GNU real32 build, dx = 2 km, dt = 12 s, 40 layers, WSM6 only) dumped by the instrumented ctessum-claude/WRF fork (module_esm_dump, esm_dump_inner hooks in mp_wsm6_run of the ctessum-claude/MMM-physics fork 52cfbd7) and replayed through the real64 (kind_phys = real64) kernels/wsm6_driver at the WRF sub-step, step 250 (t = 50 min), row j = 23, column i = 30. The only dumped inputs are the start-of-sub-step t, q, p, den, qc and the POST-SEDIMENTATION qi, qr, qs, qg (reconstructed from the dump's water and energy budgets, as in melting_freezing.esm's own tests) -- WSM6's sedimentation is an in-place semi-Lagrangian PLM update and not a rate, so no component of this repo can hand the melting/freezing block its input state; everything from there on is produced by the chain. Assertions are Linf_error over the whole 40-layer column against the dumped `<rate>_raw` rates, `<rate>_final` rates, `*_upd` state and pcond, i.e. every interface of the chain plus its end product. Nothing here is rate x dt (FORTRAN_BUGS.md N3), so the comparison is at the kernel's own sub-step. Regime: the MIXED-PHASE glaciated flank of the same storm -- snow 2.7e-3 and graupel 6.3e-3 kg/kg dominate, cloud water 4.2e-4, cloud ice 5.9e-5 and rain only 1.3e-5 kg/kg, 7 layers above 0 C. Deposition and riming, not warm rain, drive the column (praut is zero everywhere), and this is the column in which the mass-conservation rescaling actually BINDS: the rain budget is overdrawn at layers 15 and 16, where f_qr = 0.7146 and 0.5877 rescale prevp, pracw, piacr, psacr and pgacr, so the coupled document also tests that the rescaling is driven by rates the upstream stages produced rather than by dumped ones. Residual of the whole chain against the real64 replay, measured with zero tolerances (Linf over the column, as a fraction of that column's maximum): the melting/freezing outputs 0 (qs) to 3.7e-12 -- essentially exact here, because this column has no melting and only trace freezing -- xl 6.0e-9, cpm 3.4e-10, qsat_w 4.5e-7, rh_w 4.8e-7; the process rates 9.6e-8 (pgacr) to 6.1e-6 (pidep, whose sequential vapor budget subtracts three nearly cancelling terms); the rescaled rates the same, so the f_qr = 0.7146/0.5877 rescaling at layers 15 and 16 is reproduced to the same accuracy from rates the upstream stages produced; the updated state 2.1e-9 (qc) to 3.5e-7 (qi); and pcond 1.2e-5, the largest residual of either regime. Tolerances are set at a fixed fraction of each column's maximum -- 5e-8 for T and the latent heats, 5e-6 for the mixing ratios and the saturation state, 5e-5 for the process rates and 1e-4 for pcond -- i.e. 8x to 30x the measured residual.

input_qi.expr: qi_rates + np.where(t0c - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) < 0, qc_rates - qc, 0) - np.where(t0c - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) > 0, qc - qc_rates, 0)

input_qr.expr: qr_rates + psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw + np.where(t0c - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) > 0, (t_rates - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) - (xls - xl)/cpm*(qc - qc_rates))*cpm/(xls - xl), 0)

input_qg.expr: qg_rates - pgmlt_raw - np.where(t0c - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) > 0, (t_rates - (t + xlf0/cpm*(psmlt_raw + pgmlt_raw)) - (xls - xl)/cpm*(qc - qc_rates))*cpm/(xls - xl), 0)
